title: installer: add jurisdictional KMS routing and install-time audit-proof rollback hooks
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Motivation: Customers deploying Redwood Private in regulated jurisdictions require installer-time guarantees that tenant keys are pinned to allowed KMS regions and that installer failures cannot leak interim key material or leave audit gaps. This PR adds an install-time jurisdictional KMS router plus a lightweight audit-envelope signer and rollback-safe hooks so that (1) installation manifests are validated against a jurisdiction map, (2) KMS configuration is materialized with region affinity metadata, and (3) every installer step that touches KMS or audit state emits an idempotent, rollback-safe audit envelope. Summary of changes: implement manifest-level kms routing and validation; add an installer-side audit envelope signer that writes signed envelopes to the local audit store and optionally pushes to the configured audit sink; introduce rollback-safe hooks invoked by the installer to unwind KMS provisioning without losing audit continuity; add integration tests exercising cross-region rejection, fallback path to a permitted KMS provider, and installer recovery after a simulated crash. Backwards compatibility: installer will skip jurisdiction enforcement when 'jurisdictional_kms.enabled=false' for backward compat to older installs. Security notes: the local signer holds a short-lived installer ephemeral key stored in the TPM/HSM when available; installers running in air-gapped environments will generate ephemeral keys and persist envelopes to disk for later ingestion. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (ENG-2147) reviewed by security and infra - [x] Unit tests for kms router validation - [x] Integration tests for rollback semantics - [x] E2E in a hermetic env with mock KMS providers - [x] Documentation added to docs/compliance/jurisdictional-kms.md How to review: look at installer/pkg/kms/router.go for routing policy logic, installer/pkg/audit/enveloper.go for envelope format and signing guarantees, and installer/scripts/rollback-safe-hooks.sh for the steps executed during failure unwind. See integration test harness under installer/tests/integration for scenario definitions. Related work: builds on ideas from ENG-176543 (policy simulator) and SEC-502 (audit canonicalization).

review_conversation: Liam O'Connor: Overall great approach. Two concerns: 1) need to ensure deterministic envelope canonicalization so signatures verify across machines; 2) ensure we redact any transient plaintext keys from logs.
Priya Kapoor: Addressed both. Added canonicalization routine (enveloper.canonicalize) and clear-zero on ephemeral key path after signing. Updated tests to assert canonicalization output.
Marcus Li: Integration test failed first run (mock KMS timed out). Please add retry/backoff and increase mock timeouts for hermetic runs.
Priya Kapoor: Added retry/backoff with bounded jitter and increased mock timeout in test harness. Reran CI and green.
Olivia Park: Can the installer operate in an offline audit-mode where it writes envelopes only to disk? I'd like to see that explicitly called out.
Priya Kapoor: Yes — offline mode is supported via 'audit.sink=local' and documented in jurisdictional-kms.md. Added a test that verifies envelopes persisted to disk are stable across restarts.
Liam O'Connor: Approved after changes. Marcus Li: Approved. Olivia Park: Approved.
release_notes: Add install-time jurisdictional KMS routing with validation, audit-envelope signer for installer operations, and rollback-safe hooks to preserve audit continuity during failure and recovery.
